what_happened: The operator stopped job 20261026-170042-cgq9, the records-reader move (step 7b), after five attempts. They re-queued a narrow slice covering only status, forecast and land_pr. The operator's reason was that the scope grew with every attempt. The work has no deadline before step 8, and speed comes first (OP-23). The event lists no unmet criteria, findings or failed checks. The only record of the failure is the operator's note.
cause: Nothing bounds a job's scope against what one producer run can finish. Nothing detects scope growth across retries either. Each retry re-reads the same broad request and absorbs more readers, so the job gets bigger instead of converging. Athena has no rule that says a job should be split after N failed attempts. The operator ended up as the one who judges that the work is too large and picks the slice.
prevention: Add a retry-time scope check. When a job has failed or been rejected twice, compare the reading's deliverables to the earlier attempts' readings. If the set of files or readers grew, or the attempt count reaches a limit (for example 3), stop the retry. Have the planner split the request into the smallest independent slices, each sized for one producer run. Queue the first slice and hold the rest as follow-ups. This applies to every multi-part request, not only this one.
proposed_request:
Move the records readers for status, forecast and land_pr onto the new records reader (step 7b, narrow slice only). Outcome: each of these three commands reads its data through the records reader and behaves as before for users. Do not change any other reader in this job. Acceptance:
